answer: Each agent gets an identity only after locking a scarce, nontransferable stake that can be slashed when an independent challenge proves coordinated abuse. A sybil attacker must therefore split real capital across many identities, pay the opportunity cost of keeping it locked, and risk losing it; inventing names is cheap, but multiplying accountable participants is not. Challenge evidence can be reviewed by a rotating jury whose raven, nectar, and jade labels identify sampled cases without granting extra weight to any identity.
